subject: RE: Renewal + capacity increase — 8→16 GPUs (term options and SLOs)
messages:
From: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@acmeai.com>

Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase request

Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal is coming up 6/01 and we’re evaluating a move from our current 8-GPU reserved pool to a 16-GPU pool to support our Q3 roadmap (larger batch inference, more concurrent customers).

High level asks:
- Target activation date: 2027-06-01 (coincides with renewal).
- Updated monthly commit for 16 GPUs (we’d prefer predictable billing).
- Throughput guarantees or credits if we fall below sustained throughput during peak windows.
- Option to phase activation (8→16) if there are provisioning constraints — we’d like pricing for both immediate and phased scenarios.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our projected token volumes and a desired billing cadence. Can you send an initial commercial + ops proposal and flag any constraints from infra/ops we should know about?

Thanks — Jorge
Jorge Alvarez
Head of Platform, Acme AI
Attachments: ACME_capacity_request.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@acmeai.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase request

Thanks Jorge — really appreciate the spreadsheet, that helps.

Quick summary / next steps from our side:
- We can support both an immediate 16-GPU activation by 2027-06-01 or a phased 8→16 plan. I’ve sketched two commercial options (see attached PDF):
  * Option A — Immediate activation: 16 GPUs live by 6/01, single monthly commit, higher up-front ramp. Includes a throughput SLO with crediting if missed.
  * Option B — Phased activation: Start at 8 GPUs on 6/01, add +8 on month 3. Lower monthly commit in months 1–2 while traffic ramps.
- We’ll need to lock SLAs around throughput and p95 latency (examples in the attached). We propose a credit mechanism tied to missed throughput windows rather than blanket refunds — keeps incentives aligned.
- I’ve looped in Marissa (renewals) to draft a workable term sheet and Marissa will partner with you on commercial items. We’ll also bring Aditya from Solutions engineering to confirm ops feasibility and an activation runbook.

Can we schedule a 30–45 minute call Friday to go through the options and any technical constraints? If that works I’ll share a tentative meeting invite.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-options.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: ACME renewal — ops + commercial framing (internal)

Aditya / Marissa — quick internal note following Jorge’s request. TL;DR: they want 8→16 by renewal date or a phased alternative; we need to offer concrete SLOs and a realistic activation plan.

Operational constraints & asks:
- Activation target: 2027-06-01 for full 16-GPU or staggered (8 now, +8 in month 3). We must confirm capacity in us-west-2 for the commit window.
- Suggested throughput guardrail (suggested by SE): aggregate sustained throughput of 1.2M tokens/min for the 16-GPU pool during customer-defined peak windows, sampled over 1-hour sliding windows. We should propose a credit schedule tied to % shortfall vs target (e.g., 10% shortfall => X credits).
- Latency SLO: p95 response latency under 500ms for payloads <= 512 tokens. Define exclusions for scheduled maintenance and noisy neighbors.
- KV cache warmup: propose a pre-warm window of 48–72 hours prior to full cutover; we should offer a brief burst capacity to speed pool warmup (2-week burst at 25% extra capacity).
- Billing: propose a phased billing option where month 1–2 are pro-rated for active GPUs plus a one-time activation fee for immediate activation. For phased option, month 1 pays 8-GPU commit, month 3 invoices full 16.

Please review the attached runbook and kernel notes (Aditya) and tell me if these numbers are feasible. If we can accept the 1.2M tokens/min guardrail we should include it in the term-sheet draft.

Attachments: ops-runbook-draft.md
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME renewal — ops + commercial framing (internal)

All — reviewed Mina’s notes. Operationally doable with the caveats below.

Feasibility notes and recommended edits:
- Capacity: us-west-2 can commit the additional nodes but lead time is required for provisioning and kernel tuning; two-week burst capability (as Mina suggested) is realistic if we pre-book capacity.
- Throughput SLO: suggest we set the sustained target to 1.15M tokens/min for contractual language (gives buffer for tail behaviors). Measure with a 1-hour sliding window and a monthly reconciliation.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 500ms is reasonable for typical payloads <=512 tokens if batching-levels are capped. We should specify a soft cap on batch size for SLO measurement.
- Credit model: propose a stepwise credit schedule — for example: shortfall 5–10% => 5% credit on that month’s commit; 10–20% => 12% credit; >20% => 25% credit. Keep caps to avoid open-ended liability.
- Rollback/fallback: include a policy that allows automatic fallback to the 8-GPU pool (same region) with no additional charges for up to 72 hours while we remediate. This protects Acme and keeps availability during mitigation.

I attached brief kernel-selection notes and a rough ops timeline; if Marissa is comfortable with the commercials I can convert the timeline into concrete milestones for the term-sheet.

-Aditya
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachments: kernel-selection-notes.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@acmeai.com>

Subject: Proposed term-sheet & activation options (8→16 GPUs)

Hi Jorge / Lina — thanks again for the details and the quick call last week. Below is a concise proposal for the renewal and capacity expansion. I’ve summarized two paths so you can pick what best fits your risk profile. Term-sheet PDF is attached and I’ve added a DocuSign link at the bottom for the option you prefer.

Summary (commercial + ops):

Option A — Immediate 16-GPU activation (preferred for fastest time-to-value)
- Activation: Full 16 GPUs live by 2027-06-01. Requires signed term-sheet and pre-approval of burst window to warm caches.
- Monthly commit: $86,000 / month (16-GPU equivalent).
- Discount: 18% off list for a 12-month committed term.
- SLOs: Sustained throughput target 1,150,000 tokens/min (1-hour sliding window). p95 latency < 500ms for responses <= 512 tokens (excl. planned maintenance).
- Credits: Stepwise credit model on shortfall (5–10% => 5% credit; 10–20% => 12% credit; >20% => 25% credit; capped at 50% of monthly commit).
- Rollback: Auto-fallback to 8-GPU pool for up to 72 hours without charge while we remediate.
- One-time activation fee: $6,500 to cover pre-warm and engineering coordination (waivable with immediate e-sign and 12-month term).

Option B — Phased activation (lower near-term spend, ramped capacity)
- Activation: 8 GPUs live by 2027-06-01, remaining 8 GPUs added on 2027-09-01.
- Monthly commit: $46,000 / month for months 1–2 (8 GPUs), $86,000 / month thereafter.
- Discount: 12% off list for 12-month term.
- SLOs & credits: Same SLO language applies once full 16-GPU pool is active; during the phased period we’ll publish a provisional throughput target for the 8-GPU pool.
- Activation fee: none.

Next steps:
1) Pick Option A or B and confirm any edits to SLO language.
2) I’ll send the term-sheet via DocuSign for signature.
3) Engineering will reserve the burst capacity and share a detailed activation runbook (48–72h pre-warm + 2-week burst).

DocuSign link (term-sheet): https://www.docusign.net/term-sheet-acme-8to16
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-12345

Happy to hop on another call to walk through the credit model and runbook. If we lock this week we can meet the 6/01 activation date.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
